(1) fair bandwidth allocation in multi-hop WLAN networks can improve network throughput and coverage, and (2) this improvement can be achieved by decoupling the problem into two separate but complementary problems: multi-hop structure design and fair bandwidth allocation.

(1) the objective of improving the throughput without sacrificing the fairness can be better met in multi hop WLANs than in single-hop WLANs and (2) we have proposed a novel solution that achieves this improvement.

(i) multi-hop WLANs have a much higher potential for throughput improvement than single-hop WLANs; and (ii) this potential can be effectively harnessed by using a multi-hop structure that is carefully designed and a bandwidth allocation algorithm that is carefully chosen.
